concepts.definition: The source's preferred realization discipline for Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, explicit authority and effects, and prevention of interface bleed inside adopted implementation and design boundaries.

grounding.quote:
- `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` answers what is the preferred implementation design
  discipline when you want Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, no
  interface bleed, and explicit authority and effect management

concepts.label: Design Module Method

concepts.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS) names the architectural carriers distinguished from Subordinate Payloads. Carrier membership may change through accepted Ontology and design re-entry. Subordinate Payloads are shapes retained within a carrier family unless an independent boundary is justified.

grounding.quote:
The IACS is not numerically frozen. Adding, removing, merging, or splitting a
carrier is lawful through accepted Ontology and design re-entry. For every such
revision, accepted design:

- if a shape does not need independent authority, independent reuse, or direct
  pattern-match semantics, it remains a Subordinate Payload and stays nested,
  private, or local to the carrier family

concepts.label: IACS and Subordinate Payloads

concepts.definition: The Promotion Test places the burden of proof on promoting a subordinate shape into an independent top-level architectural type.

grounding.quote:
The burden of proof is on promotion.

Designers and reviewers should assume a candidate type stays subordinate until
an irreducible boundary is shown.

concepts.label: Promotion Test

concepts.definition: Boundary Inflation is design debt: promoting payload detail into peer types because typing is difficult; exposing internal records without a new authoritative boundary; producing many near-identical top-level types where one carrier family suffices; or silently turning one migration ticket into parallel schema migrations.

grounding.quote:
Boundary Inflation exists when:

- payload detail is promoted into peer types because the code feels hard to type
- internal records are turned into public schema surface without a new
  authoritative boundary
- many near-identical top-level types appear for one boundary where one carrier
  family would suffice
- one migration ticket silently becomes several parallel schema migrations

Boundary Inflation is design debt, not progress.

concepts.label: Boundary Inflation

concepts.definition: The capitalized engineering Ontology describes one designed boundary. It supplies the accepted identities, relationships, lifecycle, authority and function law from which design views derive; its use requires no adoption of a world-model or metaphysical ontology.

grounding.quote:
The capitalized `Ontology` in section 4B is the engineering Ontology of one
designed boundary. It does not require adoption of the Constraint-Emergence
Ontology, a world-model theory, or any other metaphysical or empirical claim.

concepts.label: Engineering Ontology

concepts.definition: One complete three-view design asset comprises a domain model (`classDiagram`), execution model (`sequenceDiagram`) and lifecycle model (`stateDiagram-v2`). Together these are fidelity-checked Ontology projections and the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behavior, lifecycle and axiom conformance.

grounding.quote:
The asset must contain all three views:

1. a Mermaid `classDiagram` domain model;
2. a Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` execution model; and
3. a Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` lifecycle model.

concepts.label: Three-view behavioral design

concepts.definition: Invariant Reconstruction Sufficiency is an action-and-affected-set property of existing Ontology, authority/admission relations, frame declarations, views and module mappings. It distinguishes action/relation classifications preserves, changes, duplicates and violates from evaluation verdicts and separately evaluates reconstruction sufficiency and action lawfulness.

grounding.quote:
| preserves | Operates inside the intact relation. |
| changes | Alters the relation and requires acceptance by re-entry at that relation. |
| duplicates | Establishes an equivalent path explicitly disposed as constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realization. |
| violates | Contradicts the relation, leaves an equivalent path undisposed, or accepts a changed relation only inside the acting frame. |

concepts.label: Invariant Reconstruction Sufficiency

concepts.definition: A subordinate computational realization projection exposes abstract data types, keys and identity structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, implementations and domain mappings that domain-only views can conceal. Each material component has an explicit semantic and operational role set; similarity identifies a commonization candidate, not semantic identity, ownership or authority.

grounding.quote:
**The projection.** At a material semantic boundary, the design must project
the domain design into its computational realization: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and effect
boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational mappings. The
cross-view evaluation extends to prove the domain views and this projection
describe one system.

concepts.label: Computational Realization Projection and component roles

concepts.definition: Recommended module roles are: carrier, defining typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; semantic kernel, transforming carriers without effects; effect shell, performing emission, publication, network/subprocess/persistence/operator effects; projection, deriving read models or reports from source truth; binding/adapter, converting external and internal carriers without inventing law; constructor/materialization, building artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Modules bound graph-traversal reasoning and expose recurrence candidates.

grounding.quote:
- **Carrier module**: defines typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts,
  transitions, records, or envelopes
- **Semantic kernel module**: implements the main transforms over carriers
  without performing side effects
- **Effect shell module**: performs event emission, file publication, network
  calls, subprocess execution, persistence, or operator delivery
- **Projection module**: derives read models or reports from authoritative
  source truth
- **Binding or adapter module**: converts between external boundaries and the
  project's internal carriers without inventing semantic law
- **Constructor or materialization module**: writes generated or built artifacts
  from admitted carriers and explicit plans

concepts.label: Design module roles

concepts.definition: A module-derived Unit Test is a module-owned proof lane within the product-assurance bounded context. This method owns that concept and proof relation, not Product-level UAT or acceptance meaning.

grounding.quote:
This clause consumes the product-assurance bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance` declared by
`SPEC_METHOD.md#testing-strategy-taxonomy`. `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` owns the
module-derived `Unit Test` concept and proof relation inside that context; it
does not take ownership of Product-level UAT or acceptance meaning.

Unit tests under this method are module-owned proof lanes.

They must derive from module ownership evidence, not from code shape alone.

concepts.label: Module-derived Unit Test

concepts.definition: Module lifecycle confirmation detects ambiguity about ultimate intended use at each governed realization boundary. It consumes the Spec Method's canonical operational lifecycle without redefining phases, and is neither a release plan nor a replacement for Release Method.

grounding.quote:
The canonical operational lifecycle chain is defined by `SPEC_METHOD.md` under
the Operational Lifecycle Sufficiency Rule. This method consumes that canonical
chain; it does not redefine the phases.

This checklist is not a release plan and does not replace `RELEASE_METHOD.md`.
It is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.

concepts.label: Module lifecycle confirmation

concepts.definition: Governance surfaces describe state, boundaries and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should perform work. Strategy ownership and explicitly owned assessment are instance-specific ratified responsibilities and grants, not consequences of accurate observation.

grounding.quote:
The required distinction is:

- governance surfaces describe the state, boundary, and admissible routes
- strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should do the work

concepts.label: Governance and strategy surfaces

concepts.definition: A recurrence/commonization candidate is a repeated realization pattern across processed boundaries, usually authority-neutral, not Product truth, reused across at least two tickets or boundaries and consumable through local adapters. Examples include expectation derivation, nested contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect-edge plans and constructors that do not own semantic law.

grounding.quote:
A recurrence candidate is usually:

- not product truth
- authority-neutral
- reused across two or more tickets or module boundaries
- consumable through local adapters without changing semantic ownership

Typical candidates include:

- expectation derivation
- nested contract or policy carriers
- proof-helper or fixture shaping
- effect-edge request or plan shaping
- constructor or materialization helpers that do not own semantic law

concepts.label: Recurrence candidate

concepts.definition: A proxy interface is a new-looking surface forwarding to an old authority path, reconstructing missing truth from it, keeping it executable under a new name or preserving green proofs while old law governs. The source classifies this as bridge debt.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that:

- forwards to the old authority path
- reconstructs missing truth from the old path
- keeps the old path executable behind a new name
- allows proofs to stay green while the old law still governs

This is bridge debt, not progress.

concepts.label: Proxy interface

concepts.definition: STDO Foundations declares commitments for purposeful construction by finite-resource actors and shared decisions about results, current state, bounded work, authority conservation, independent assessment and construction assurance. Its bounded context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:foundations, owned by the STDO Specification Methodology Product authority.

grounding.quote:
The core owns the shared decisions about results, current state, bounded work,
authority conservation, required independent assessment and construction assurance. Particular methods supply domain predicates, types,
policies and authority bindings. They apply those decisions without maintaining
parallel rules. A specialization does not assign unrelated software or calculus
definitions a common purpose, signature or workflow.

The declared bounded context is `urn:stdo:bounded-context:foundations`.
Its owner is the STDO Specification Methodology Product authority.

concepts.label: STDO Foundations bounded context

concepts.definition: F1 adopts purpose and adequacy with owner-selected values; F2 binds interpretation to subject and basis; F3 distinguishes scoped identity, persistent current state, representation and historical observation; F4 conserves material outer contracts under compatible typed composition and declared loss; F5 binds finite resources and truthful unknown/inadequate/interrupted handling; F6 separates evidence from owner-bound operation and decision authority.

grounding.quote:
| F1 Purpose | Adopt a selected outcome and adequacy relation for purposeful construction. Value choices come from the purpose owner. | A local successful operation need not satisfy the selected outcome. |
| F2 Interpretation | Claims are interpreted on a declared subject and basis; unsupported interpretation remains unresolved. | Encoding or structural validity is not semantic evidence. |
| F3 Identity and current state | Work has scoped identity and observable persistent state; representation and historical observation are separate. | Re-entry need not recreate completed work, and history need not describe current effects. |
| F4 Typed composition | A composite conserves its outer contract's material relations under declared compatibility and loss. | Shared machinery does not merge owners, findings or authority. |
| F5 Finite capacity and total handling | Actor resources are finite; the selected control domain admits truthful handling of unknown, inadequate and interrupted conditions. | Total handling is not omniscience, universal idempotence or guaranteed solution. |
| F6 Evidence and authority | Evidence supports claims; operation and decision authority come from their bound owners. | A judgment or available tool is not permission. |

concepts.label: F1–F6

concepts.definition: Representation is encoding; interpretation relates encoding to meaning in a declared context. Equal encodings may mean different things, and different encodings may express the same scoped meaning.

grounding.quote:
A representation is an encoding. An interpretation relates that encoding to
meaning under a declared context. Equal encodings can have different meanings;
different encodings can represent the same scoped meaning. A parser, structural
validator or successful join does not establish interpretation fidelity.

concepts.label: Interpretation and representation

concepts.definition: Scoped identity distinguishes an object; work state is the current construction subject; events, assessments and receipts evidence scoped observations or judgments; acceptance is an owner decision. These are distinct standings.

grounding.quote:
[Identity Method](IDENTITY_METHOD.md) owns governed names and coordinate changes.
Work state is the current subject under construction. An event, assessment or
receipt is evidence of a scoped observation or judgment. Acceptance is an owner
decision. None of these substitutes for another. Historical evidence remains
historical when current premises change. Reuse follows
[Change impact and evidence retention](#change-impact-and-evidence-retention),
using the current subject acquired under [Workspace and context](#workspace-and-context).

concepts.label: Identity, state, evidence and acceptance

concepts.definition: Reference-only authority vocabulary imported from the reference-frame-evaluation context comprises frame-set authority (human declaring/accepting the project frame set), semantic authority (meaning owner), evaluation authority (evaluation permission), operation authority (owner-issued construction/transformation/admission/publication/mutation grant where evaluation performs operations), decision authority (permitted result disposition), and actor identity (human, agent, tool or process doing work). These remain owner-qualified references, not local redefinitions.

grounding.quote:
| frame-set authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the human authority that declares or accepts the project frame set |
| semantic authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the owner of meaning for a material relation |
| evaluation authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the role permitted to perform an evaluation |
| operation authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish, or mutate a material subject where an evaluation performs such an operation |
| decision authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the role permitted to accept, reject, or otherwise dispose its result |
| actor identity | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the human, agent, tool, or process performing work. |

concepts.label: Owner-qualified authority imports

concepts.definition: Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts respectively specify a transformation, explain interpreted distinctions and preservation, and realize operations in software/hardware, human communication or mixed environments with material effects and resource costs. They are simultaneous accounts, not SDLC stages. A, I and C_H name proposed categories only after their structures and laws are supplied.

grounding.quote:
Keep three accounts distinct. An algorithmic account specifies the selected
transformation. An informational account explains interpreted distinctions and
their preservation. A computational account realises the operation through a concrete execution
environment: software and hardware, people and communication, or a mixed
process, with the effects and resource costs material to its obligations. They are
simultaneous descriptions, not successive SDLC stages.

concepts.label: Orthogonal descriptions

concepts.definition: Bind, Acquire, Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose are shared conditional contract vocabulary owned by the Transformation Library and specialized by methods through their types, predicates and authority. They are neither six compulsory stages nor six runtime APIs.

grounding.quote:
The [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) describes Bind, Acquire,
Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose. The library defines a shared contract vocabulary with conditional obligations
for this selected method domain. Particular methods specialize it through their
own types, predicates and authority; it is not six compulsory stages or six
runtime APIs. No operation authority follows from a contract definition.
A changed detailed determination still returns to its owning contract.

concepts.label: Canonical transformation contracts

concepts.definition: A core result claims one predicate on one exact subject and basis, retaining verdict, performance, qualified original domain outcome, evidence/citations, unresolved obligations and material effect observations. Verdicts are exactly satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis. Performance is performed, not_performed or unconfirmed. Effects use not_requested, not_started, completed, partial, reverted or unknown. These coordinates answer different questions.

grounding.quote:
A result makes a claim about one predicate on one subject and basis. Its core
record contains the predicate, exact subject and basis, verdict, performance,
original qualified domain outcome, supporting evidence and citations, unresolved
obligations and material effect observations. A reference can carry these when
its resolution preserves their meaning and availability. This is a semantic
contract, not a mandatory serialization format or additional work carrier.

concepts.label: Core result algebra

concepts.definition: Result conjunction evaluates all contract-required predicates and material joins on a composite subject and basis. Its aggregate is another core result retaining authenticated contributions, predicate mappings, cited failures, uncovered coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators; a summary never replaces them.

grounding.quote:
Conjunction evaluates whether all required predicates and their material joins
hold on the declared composite subject and basis. It retains the contributing
results, their authentication and predicate mapping, known failures and their
citations, uncovered required coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators.
The aggregate is another result in the same algebra, with those components
available through sufficient references. Its summary never replaces them.

concepts.label: Result conjunction

concepts.definition: Construction assurance binds an obligation, interpreted predicate, subject, basis, assumptions and admissible evidence. Its subrelations address preservation at joins, assertions and observations at evaluation, dependence and risk at evidence selection, and applicability at change/reuse, without creating another stage, role, record or authority.

grounding.quote:
An assurance consumer binds the selected obligation, interpreted predicate,
subject, governing basis, assumptions and admissible evidence. Apply the
subrelations below at the decision that relies on them: preservation at a
construction join, assertion and observation justification at evaluation,
dependence and risk at evidence selection, and applicability at change or reuse.
The consumer supplies its domain policy and required assurance; these shared
relations create no additional evaluation stage, role, record or authority.
Every conclusion uses the [result algebra](#result-algebra), and required
predicates combine under [result conjunction](#result-conjunction).

concepts.label: Construction assurance

concepts.definition: For obligation r, Q_r = interpret(r, Gamma, Omega) is the required predicate over cases including material inputs, behavior and environment. Assertion q_t may target Q_r or a narrower condition. Observation map pi: Omega → O and evaluation relation T contained in O × R describe available observations and admitted core-result conclusions.

grounding.quote:
For an owning obligation r, let Q_r = interpret(r, Gamma, Omega) be its required
predicate over a declared case domain Omega. A case includes material inputs,
behaviour and environment. Justify this interpretation with its conditions,
exceptions and permitted alternatives. A source identifier or digest establishes
which text was selected, not that Q_r expresses it faithfully.

concepts.label: Assertion and observation relations

concepts.definition: Assertion provenance records obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies supporting an expected predicate. Execution provenance records the actual checker, exact subject, environment, inputs, observations and result. Mutual assurance compares justified constructions/assertions within scope while accounting for shared error causes.

grounding.quote:
Assertion provenance identifies the owning obligation, interpretation,
assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies that justify the expected
predicate. Execution provenance identifies the actual checker, exact subject,
applicable environment, inputs, acquired observations and result. Preserve both
relations in existing bindings and evidence; execution logs cannot justify an
expected answer's derivation. A shared derivation can serve a declared family
without a separate document for every test.

concepts.label: Parallel assurance and provenance

concepts.definition: Risk and assurance selection chooses evidence strategies for required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits under admitted work authority. Quantified assurance is relative to declared uncertainty models, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits.

grounding.quote:
The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects assurance for the
required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits. Bind
coverage, uncertainty and the conditions for action or acceptance. More evidence
strengthens a claim only within its applicability and dependence account;
test counts or an assumed preference for more checks supply neither. Required
safety, authority and acceptance conditions remain applicable to every selected
strategy.

concepts.label: Risk and assurance selection

conditions: For every addition, removal, merge or split of a carrier.

grounding.quote:
- re-derives the complete IACS and classifies every addition, removal, merge,
  and split;
- reruns the Promotion Test and Boundary Inflation prohibition over the full
  revised set, not only newly introduced carriers;
- updates every conformance or checker subject to the declared composite
  carrier relation under `SPEC_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-022`; and
- reconciles implementation to the revised set before promotion or closure.

This obligation consumes the federal assurance law without restating it. A
prohibition without a lawful revision path is false. A revision is also false
if its gates inspect only new carriers, its assurance surfaces retain a weaker
or obsolete subject, or implementation is not reconciled before closure.

constraints.statement: Accepted design must rederive the complete IACS, classify every change, rerun Promotion and Boundary Inflation checks over the entire revised set, update every conformance/checker subject to the declared composite carrier relation under STDO-UP-022, and reconcile implementation before promotion or closure. The source calls a prohibition without lawful revision false, and likewise a revision checking only new carriers, retaining weaker/obsolete assurance subjects, or lacking implementation reconciliation before closure.
constraints.uncertainty: STDO-UP-022 and the consumed federal assurance law are not supplied.

conditions: A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record is proposed.
For promotion of a Subordinate Payload.

grounding.quote:
A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum, or named schema record must
justify its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as payload
detail.

A Subordinate Payload may be promoted to a top-level type only when at least
one of the following is true:

- it is an authoritative source carrier
- it is a public or persisted contract boundary
- it is an explicit variant of a public outcome family that consumers
  pattern-match directly
- it is reused across multiple modules without semantic bleed
- it is versioned, published, or admitted independently

Promotion is not lawful when the candidate type is only:

- internal record detail of one larger carrier
- a field grouping used once inside one module
- a temporary typing shim around an open dict
- a private payload variation that never crosses a true interface boundary
- a mirror of another type with cosmetic or local field differences

constraints.statement: Every listed top-level type must justify an architectural boundary. Promotion requires at least one of: authoritative source carriage; public/persisted contract boundary; directly pattern-matched explicit public outcome variant; multi-module reuse without semantic bleed; independent versioning, publication or admission. Promotion is unlawful for candidates that are only internal record detail, once-used field grouping, an open-dict typing shim, non-interface private variation, or a cosmetic/local mirror. Without need for independent authority, independent reuse or direct pattern matching, the shape remains nested/private/local subordinate payload. Promotion bears the proof burden; designers and reviewers should presume subordination until an irreducible boundary is shown.
constraints.uncertainty: The listed necessary alternatives are not interpreted as automatically sufficient acceptance.

conditions: Schema work.
Additionally, a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types.

grounding.quote:
Schema work must declare:

- the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set
- which types are authoritative
- which types are downstream projections
- which shapes are Subordinate Payloads
- which Subordinate Payloads are intentionally deferred from promotion

This rule exists to stop type proliferation from turning one migration into many
parallel schema migrations.

If a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types, it must distinguish:

- the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set
- Subordinate Payloads

Failing to make that distinction is design drift.

Typed closure does not excuse Boundary Inflation.

constraints.statement: Declare the IACS, authoritative types, downstream projections, subordinate shapes and intentionally deferred promotions. Wide type families must distinguish IACS from subordinate payloads; failure is design drift. Typed closure supplies no exception to the Boundary Inflation prohibition.

conditions: A realization derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.

grounding.quote:
The minimum lawful design assets for a reference-derived module boundary are:

- the named reference design surfaces being used as source material
- the accepted target Ontology, including the disposition of reference entities,
  functions, lifecycle, authority, effects, and projections
- the target design surfaces that replace or bind those source surfaces
- an explicit mapping that says what is preserved, reshaped, deferred, or
  demoted to delivery binding in the target line
- the target module boundary assets required by this method, including the
  Ontology-derived Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set and three-view design
  asset

constraints.statement: Completion must not rest on code comparison alone. Required derivation evidence runs from constitutional WHAT through reference design, target Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping, target design mapping, target module boundary assets and implementation. Assets name source design surfaces, accepted target Ontology with dispositions of reference entities/functions/lifecycle/authority/effects/projections, replacement or binding target surfaces, explicit preserved/reshaped/deferred/delivery-demoted mappings, and Ontology-derived IACS plus three-view design. The question is derivation of the target boundary without incidental implementation drift; inability to show that chain means not yet design-method complete.
constraints.uncertainty: The constitutional and reference surfaces themselves are not supplied.

conditions: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary.
exceptions: Unchanged boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realization work without material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate the gate.

grounding.quote:
Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary must carry
one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset before
the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure. When
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, design evidence, implementation, and tests
may develop together before that gate. Otherwise the affected unresolved,
contradictory, or materially non-equivalent relation is accepted before
retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged boundaries cite their
accepted basis; local realization work with no material semantic-boundary delta
does not recreate this gate.

constraints.statement: Require one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view asset before promotion or design-method closure. Co-development of design, implementation and tests is permitted when co_evolution_admissible(B) holds. Otherwise acceptance of the affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation precedes retained implementation establishing it. Views are substantive fidelity-checked projections, not decorative or peer truth surfaces.
constraints.uncertainty: The full definition of co_evolution_admissible(B) is outside the supplied sections.

conditions: For the active boundary's design asset.
exceptions: Composition and effect algebra are required where applicable.
constraints.statement: Cite one accepted Ontology and include or reference entity/relationship inventory, invariant/cardinality law, lifecycle completeness matrix, authority matrix, atomic/higher-order-function derivation matrix, applicable composition/effect algebra, whole-family Prime contraction with every accepted atom's admitted domain and realization-projection mapping, and explicit deferred/excluded/unresolved functionality.
constraints.uncertainty: Prime and the complete atom law are referenced but not defined here.

conditions: A proposed bounded action and accepted material-frame basis.
Lawfulness is evaluated separately when action conformance is assessed.

grounding.quote:
Evaluate two named predicates separately through the core result record:
"the selected method and accepted design suffice to reconstruct the governing
relations and classify action A on affected set M" and, when action conformance
is assessed, "A is lawful against those relations." Demonstrated complete
reconstruction satisfies the first even when the recovered action classification
is `violates`; an established missing material relation or indistinguishable
required case falsifies it. Unexamined support or an undecided distinction is
indeterminate. The lawfulness predicate is satisfied by supported `preserves`,
by `changes` with the required accepted re-entry, or by `duplicates` with its
required explicit disposition; a demonstrated `violates` falsifies it.
A proposed change or duplicate without decided acceptance/disposition retains
indeterminate lawfulness unless evidence already establishes a violation.
Unusable subject/basis and established scope/capability shortfall retain
invalid_basis and out_of_frame on the affected predicate. Preserve the action
classification, reason, performance and evidence; a label without its required
support establishes neither predicate.

constraints.statement: Apply the referenced Contract application to the action and basis. Selected STDO method supplies required relations/deciding laws; accepted design supplies concrete values, with neither substituting for the other or repetition counting as reconstruction. Recover every governing relation in the causally closed affected set. Preserves operates inside an intact relation; changes requires accepted re-entry at the changed relation; duplicates requires explicit constituent/replica/replacement/deliberately-independent disposition; violates contradicts a relation, leaves an equivalent path undisposed, or accepts change only inside the acting frame. Complete reconstruction satisfies sufficiency even for violates; established missing material relations or indistinguishable required cases falsify it; unexamined support/undecided distinctions are indeterminate. Lawfulness follows supported preservation, accepted change or disposed duplication; demonstrated violation falsifies it. Undecided proposed change/duplication remains indeterminate absent established violation. Invalid subject/basis and scope/capability shortfall retain invalid_basis/out_of_frame. Preserve classification, reason, performance and evidence. This is an existing-artifact property limited to the declared action/set, not future changes or reviewer performance. Sufficiency testing uses named independently known cases/decisions while withholding conversation, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore; these cannot supply missing governing relations.
constraints.uncertainty: The external Contract application and material-frame binding are not fully supplied.

conditions: The active boundary's domain model.
exceptions: Atomic function inputs/outputs are shown where they cross the active boundary.
Higher-order composition is shown where it determines boundary shape.
constraints.statement: The structural projection must show domain identities/cardinalities, ownership/invariants/lawful lifecycle relations, applicable atomic inputs/outputs and higher-order compositions, IACS/Prime mappings, subordinate and effect-edge payloads, downstream projections, deferred families, authority/downstream roles, visibility and actual relationship structure. Standard stereotypes are <<prime-conformant>>, <<subordinate>>, <<effect-edge>>, <<deferred>>, <<authoritative>>, <<downstream>>. Visibility is + for public/exported and - for module-local/private. Standard relationship expectations use composition for owned subordinate payloads, association for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant/outcome families.

conditions: The sequence model.
Malformed input/output, retry, recursion, fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow and human escalation paths are required where applicable.
exceptions: A participant may be an explicitly external actor instead of an entity in the domain model.

grounding.quote:
Every participant must exist in the domain model or be an explicitly external
actor. Every message must bind to a declared carrier transform, graph/C
constructor, interpreter action, or effect-handler call. A private loop,
service method, plugin, shell, or script may not silently replace a declared
workflow transition.

Every message must also bind to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
role. Actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorize a message.

constraints.statement: Show supported execution from admitted input to result or truthful stop, naming owner and required authority for every decision, admission, execution, projection and effect boundary, plus applicable exceptional and composite paths. Every participant must be in the domain model or explicitly external. Every message binds both to a declared carrier transform, graph/C constructor, interpreter action or effect-handler call and to an Ontology function with admitted authority role. Private loops, services, plugins, shells or scripts cannot silently replace workflow transitions; actor identity/reachability cannot authorize messages.
constraints.uncertainty: The cross-view requirement later says every sequence participant exists in the domain model without repeating the external-actor exception.

conditions: The active boundary's state model.
The controller-memory restriction applies when the Product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership.

grounding.quote:
The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities. It must
show the complete admitted lifecycle for the active boundary, including
refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation, and terminal states that the
boundary can produce. Every transition must bind to an Ontology function and
name its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection,
or external act.

Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
product declares replay, event, graph, or carrier ownership.

constraints.statement: Show the complete admitted lifecycle, including every producible refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal state. Every transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act. Controller-local memory cannot supply lifecycle truth under declared replay/event/graph/carrier ownership.

conditions: Evaluation of every applicable product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axiom on a named design boundary and governing basis.

grounding.quote:
Only supported applicability results determine exclusions. The conformance
gate retains those results as coverage evidence; it does not conjoin a true
exclusion's falsified applicability predicate as if it were a failed required
axiom. Unresolved applicability keeps coverage unresolved.

constraints.statement: Keep applicability and conformance separate. Original pass maps to satisfied with evidence, fail to falsified with counterexample; supported not_applicable falsifies applicability under its owning law and gives no conformance judgment. Unsupported exclusion is indeterminate and cannot remove required coverage. Missing decisive evidence is indeterminate, unusable basis invalid_basis, and applicable scope/capability shortfall out_of_frame, not exclusion. Preserve legal performance pairs: interrupted undertaken evaluation remains performed with extent/counterexample; never undertaken is not_performed; uncertain execution is unconfirmed. Supported exclusions remain coverage evidence, not failed required conjuncts. Minimum columns are axiom/evaluated predicate, exact subject/basis, Ontology evidence, authority, domain/sequence/state evidence, native enforcement, admission/compiler enforcement, original domain outcome, core verdict, performance/extent, effects, residual/gap owner. Columns may resolve existing records; preserve original label, selected predicate and reasoned applicability. Bare labels are incomplete handoffs.

conditions: Cross-view evaluation.
Graph visibility requirements additionally apply to graph-native work.

grounding.quote:
- every public operation is a projection of an Ontology function rather than an
  independently authored semantic peer;
- raw probabilistic output cannot transition directly to accepted or closed;
- handlers and plugins own interiors only when the runtime owns admission,
  events, continuation, and closure;
- native types enforce locally decidable relations; and
- admission or semantic compilation owns global references, completeness, and
  realization gaps.

For graph-native work, every batch, retry, recursion, or nested workflow must
be visible through the product's declared graph or compute algebra. A relied-on
`semantic_not_realized` constructor is a blocking gap. It may not be replaced
by imperative glue in a plugin, shell, service, script, or test harness.

constraints.statement: Prove every view element derives from accepted Ontology; every discovered functionality row is derived/deferred/excluded/gap-disposed; every sequence participant and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every message has a semantic/effect boundary; every lifecycle transition derives from admitted truth; every function/transition has an explicit authority path with no implicit widening by composition; every public operation projects an Ontology function. Raw probabilistic output cannot directly become accepted/closed. Handler/plugin interior ownership requires runtime ownership of admission, events, continuation and closure. Native types enforce locally decidable relations; admission/semantic compilation owns global references, completeness and realization gaps. Graph-native batches, retries, recursion and nested workflows must appear through declared graph/compute algebra. A relied-on semantic_not_realized constructor blocks and cannot be replaced by imperative plugin/shell/service/script/test glue.
constraints.uncertainty: External sequence actors create a localized reading issue retained separately.

conditions: At the design gate.
Promotion/closure requirements apply to new or semantically changed boundaries.
exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor reuses accepted Ontology/design, identifies touched projections and proves no delta in entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority, functions, effects and public semantics; it creates no new Ontology or acceptance ceremony.

grounding.quote:
At the gate, apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application)
to the admissibility of the exact design assessment and its support. Conjoin
the required Ontology, design-view, constructability and axiom results for the
design-conformance predicate. The design authority separately records its
`accepted` or `non-accepted` decision. An acceptance decision requires the
satisfied conformance result and the authority's lawful mandate; non-acceptance
retains the actual failed, unresolved or diagnosed conformance result and does
not itself mean falsified. Evaluate the lawfulness of either decision through
the core [decision predicate](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra), preserving the
decision and its reason. No view count, empty set or supported exclusion
substitutes for the required assessment coverage.

For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design decisions must
both be `accepted` before the affected implementation, public contract, or
semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method closure. Any
failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition, unresolved
authority path, or blocking realization gap keeps the decision non-accepted.

constraints.statement: Assess exact assessment/support admissibility, conjoin required Ontology, views, constructability and axioms, and separately record accepted/non-accepted with decision-lawfulness evaluation. Acceptance requires satisfied conformance and lawful mandate. Non-acceptance preserves failed, unresolved or diagnosed conformance and does not itself mean falsified. View counts, empty sets or exclusions do not replace coverage. Both Ontology/design decisions must be accepted before affected implementation/contracts/carriers are promoted or closure claimed. Failed applicable axioms, missing functionality dispositions, unresolved authority paths and blocking realization gaps require non-acceptance. Assets stay boundary-bounded; unrelated bootstrap, harness, projection or delivery shapes added merely for apparent completeness are defects. Missing Ontology, any view, cross-view evaluation or either acceptance decision means incomplete; affected promotion, publication and closure remain forbidden.

conditions: Implementation before or alongside design evidence, including retrospective review.
exceptions: Only a disposable spike may cross an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before acceptance when co_evolution_admissible(B) does not hold.

grounding.quote:
When `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, implementation may precede or develop
with design evidence and may be retained after reconciliation. Until the
design gate is accepted, it is provisional evidence: it does not author
semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or closure.
Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected unresolved,
contradictory, or materially non-equivalent relation before design acceptance.

Existing implementation placed under retrospective review may continue to
inform the affected design. Co-evolution remains lawful only while
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds; newly discovered material ambiguity,
contradiction, or materially non-equivalent network makes
`decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that decision.
Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the required
Ontology, three-view asset, and axiom evaluation are accepted. The design must
evaluate the code against prior authority; it must not rewrite the Ontology or
diagrams merely to rationalize an unlawful implementation shape.

constraints.statement: When co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, implementation may precede/develop with evidence and be retained after reconciliation. Before gate acceptance it is provisional evidence without semantic, publication, promotion or closure authority. Existing code may inform retrospective design, but newly discovered material ambiguity, contradiction or materially non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and gates that decision. Closure/promotion await accepted Ontology, three-view asset and evaluation. Assess code against prior authority; do not rationalize unlawful implementation by rewriting Ontology or diagrams. Continuing work with missing gate assets is provisional only while the co-evolution predicate holds.
constraints.uncertainty: Complete definitions of the two named predicates are not supplied.

conditions: Every material realization component and material semantic boundary.
Material producer-to-consumer paths include method and assurance operations where material.
exceptions: Behavior already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation and does not require re-entry.
Software-module mechanics apply where software realizes the boundary, not as a requirement to encode every human step.

grounding.quote:
A component may lawfully hold several roles. Three cases must be distinguished:
behavior already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are each
design changes. Only the latter two require re-entry. Use of a component
outside its declared role set must not silently establish identity, admission,
lifecycle, ordering, closure, or projection truth.

constraints.statement: Declare each component's semantic/operational roles; capability grants no authority. Multiple roles are lawful, but a new operational responsibility or semantic/authoritative role requires design re-entry, and use outside roles cannot silently establish identity/admission/lifecycle/ordering/closure/projection truth. Preserve applicable authority under supporting STDO-UP-004. Project material boundaries into computational structure and prove agreement with domain views. Tenant binding states operations, composition, effects, authority and material resource measures with units/observation boundaries for machine, human or mixed processes. Human operations retain input/outcome/refusal/recovery contracts; role titles are not implementations. For material producer-consumer paths identify fact establishment, consumers, basis/invalidators, effects, retained alternatives and accumulated work under referenced validity/reuse and enclosing-admission laws. Local success cannot establish a complete-path claim; different names cannot establish different computational responsibilities.
constraints.uncertainty: STDO-UP-004, tenant binding, workspace validity/reuse and UP-021 are externally owned and incompletely supplied.

conditions: Material algorithmic work and each material algorithmic obligation in M(B).
exceptions: Independent implementations may be justified by stated isolation, substrate, performance, security or dependency-ownership constraints.

grounding.quote:
**Disposition is two-part.** Each material algorithmic obligation in `M(B)`
carries a *semantic disposition* — existing accepted relation, extension, or
new candidate relation — and a *realization disposition* — consume, implement
locally, optimize, adapt, or deliberately duplicate under stated non-semantic
constraints. Isolation, substrate, performance, security, and dependency
ownership are each lawful grounds for an independent implementation.

The invariant is not that equivalent code is never rebuilt. It is that a local
realization must not present an existing accepted semantic or authoritative
relation as newly owned local truth.

constraints.statement: Declare supported input dimensions, workload/growth and operational assumptions; bind Product-owned acceptance limits/authority before qualification. Challenge representative supported paths and material growth; observe work directly where elapsed time cannot locate it without rerunning merely to count. Separate material startup/framework/external-compute/transport/assurance costs; use existing surfaces, with no extra accounting system or fixed complexity required. Similarity only proposes commonization, followed by semantic/operational equivalence evaluation and reuse, parameterized relation or justified separation. Compare identity/key law, ownership, ordering, mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure, access, lifecycle and truth authority. Materially non-equivalent laws require separation; other differences justify it only if parameterization/adaptation weakens ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints. Difference alone does not discharge Prime/recurrence review. Every obligation has semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, new candidate) and realization disposition (consume, local implementation, optimize, adapt, deliberate duplication). False cases include materially equivalent ADTs/algorithms without semantic disposition, generic blocks becoming semantic authority, superficial commonization across different identity/ordering/failure/ownership/lifecycle laws, and local claiming of existing accepted truth.
constraints.uncertainty: M(B), Prime and upstream qualification/retention definitions are not fully supplied.

grounding.quote:
This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite.

The rules in this file remain engineering law even where the Markov-object
construct is irrelevant, unavailable, or still only candidate-class. The
theoretical framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the scope of the
method.

constraints.statement: The method stands operationally on its own without world-model adoption or empirical/metaphysical commitments. The cited Markov object is a candidate stable self-bounding identity-bearing cut separating identity-load-bearing from context-load-bearing features. Theoretical analogies associate IACS with the smallest identity-bearing cut, promotion with sufficient independent boundary authority, inflation with mistaking fragments for peer objects, and strong boundary typing with avoiding fuzzy/reconstructed/controller-owned identity. These analogies add no prerequisite or scope, even when the construct is irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class.
constraints.uncertainty: WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md and the full Markov-object account are not supplied; the analogy is not treated as an equivalence proof.

conditions: When the method governs a realization boundary.

grounding.quote:
When this method governs a realization boundary, modules should be classified by
role.

Recommended roles are:

constraints.statement: Modules should be classified by role using the recommended taxonomy. The purpose is a stable ownership cut for reviewers, maintainers and refactoring under finite context, attention and time, improving constrained traversal and visibility of reusable computations; it is not a naming ceremony or a guarantee of correct traversal.

conditions: New or materially changed realization boundaries.
exceptions: Unchanged realization_refactor cites accepted relations and proves no material semantic-boundary delta instead of recreating evidence.

grounding.quote:
The first chain is semantic derivation. The second is evidence feedback and
cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer. When
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, the two chains may proceed together without
making implementation semantic authority. Design still owns the structural
`HOW`. Where `decision_complete(B)` is false, the relation is design-gated at
the smallest causally closed affected decision set and retained implementation
follows its acceptance. An unchanged `realization_refactor` cites the accepted
relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not recreate
the evidence.

constraints.statement: Semantic derivation runs constitutional WHAT/requirements → Ontology/IACS/target design/three views → implementation and module-derived tests → reconciliation/acceptance → promotion/closure. Implementation/tests feed evidence, counterexamples or falsification back to affected design/Ontology, without selecting or accepting semantic answers; design owns structural HOW. Co-evolution may run both chains when admissible; otherwise an incomplete decision gates the smallest causally closed affected set before retained implementation. Final code traces to accepted Ontology and design/module assets; tests trace to ownership; implementation-first discoveries reconcile into Ontology/views before promotion/closure; unrealized constructors cannot be compensated by hidden controllers/authority paths. Tests discovered from behavior must have closure proof re-expressed against ownership. Minimum evidence: WHAT, accepted Ontology, target design, module assets/IACS, accepted three projections plus axiom evaluation, implementation and tests derived from the same Ontology/module boundary. A reference realization additionally requires reference design, target Ontology/reference mapping and target design mapping. Skipping boundary reconstruction between design/code and tests is too weak. Probabilistic/agentic construction uses Spec's owned execution relation; this method supplies frame/admission/reconstruction/computational/module evidence, not a second protocol.
constraints.uncertainty: The Spec Agentic Construction Execution protocol is referenced, not supplied or executed.

conditions: Unit tests under this method and module closure.
exceptions: Helper-level tests are permitted but cannot become canonical module-boundary proof.
Transitional slice-gating tests may exist but cannot replace module-derived unit proof.

grounding.quote:
Apply [Parallel assurance and provenance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-assurance-and-provenance)
with the accepted module obligations as assertion sources and the actual
module realisation as the executed subject. The ownership trace justifies the
source selection; [Assertions and observations](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observations)
governs the predicate it can establish and the observations needed. A test
discovered from implementation is re-expressed and justified against that
module obligation before it supplies module closure. Shared derivations and
execution records remain in the existing proof carriers.

constraints.statement: Tests must derive from ownership evidence, using accepted module obligations as assertion sources and actual realization as executed subject. Implementation-discovered tests must be justified/re-expressed against obligations before closure; shared derivations/execution records stay in existing proof carriers. Tests should trace to accepted Ontology and relevant entity/lifecycle/authority/function/effect/projection law, module design, active IACS/equivalent inventory, bounded three views and owned requirement families. They must not be authored primarily from helpers, private methods, incidental branches, temporary decomposition or mocks hiding contracts. Module-owned tests are authoritative for module proof; integration/scenario/sandbox lanes remain downstream. Code without a module-derived unit lane is not closure-ready.
constraints.uncertainty: The broader product-assurance context and UAT meaning remain externally owned.

conditions: Every designed module, function, application/runtime/plugin surface, public interface, data surface, graph function or GTL module.
Before design-method closure.
exceptions: A lifecycle phase may be declared not applicable with a reason.
Missing lifecycle truth permits proceeding only when the gap is explicitly governed.

grounding.quote:
Each lifecycle phase must be one of:

- answered by the active design, requirement, release, deployment, or telemetry
  surface
- declared not applicable with a reason
- recorded as a named `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` item with an owning follow-up

A phase list without answers, not-applicable reasons, or named gaps is not
design-method evidence.

constraints.statement: Confirm lifecycle signal at each governed boundary. Evidence states or points to upstream intent/requirement authority, build/realization, assurance/proof, release/packaging, deployment/install, live use/invocation, telemetry/projection/monitoring, retirement/revocation/supersession/decommission, and lifecycle decision owner/source truth/authority. Each phase is answered, reasonedly inapplicable, or named Gap:/Unanswered: with owning follow-up; a bare phase list is insufficient. Implementation, tests, artifacts and fixtures confirm only within declared authority and cannot invent it. Missing release/deployment/live-use/telemetry/retirement truth allows progress only under explicit gap governance; closure cannot rely on local convention, precedent, mutable runtime state, prompt prose or test-only fixtures.
constraints.uncertainty: The canonical lifecycle phases and release decisions are owned by unsupplied method surfaces.

conditions: Source-truth carriage and mutable carrier design.
exceptions: Typed immutability is preferred unless mutation is materially necessary.

grounding.quote:
Source truth should be carried in typed immutable values unless mutation is
materially necessary.

Preferred shape:

- constructor or parser produces a typed carrier
- transforms consume one carrier and return another carrier or a closed result
- projections read those carriers without mutating them

Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification when it is:

- performance-critical
- required by the host runtime or framework
- modeling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth

Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values. Preferred flow is constructor/parser → typed carrier → transforms returning carriers or closed results → nonmutating projections. Mutable state requires explicit justification when performance-critical, runtime/framework-required or modeling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth. Convenience is insufficient.
constraints.uncertainty: The enumerated justification cases are not strengthened into an exhaustive permission list.

conditions: Semantic functions and assessed method-boundary outcomes.
exceptions: Totality is a preference bounded by what the language and problem allow.
Typed explicit failure is preferred where practical.

grounding.quote:
For an assessed method-boundary outcome, bind the actual function predicate:
an established intended result satisfies it; demonstrated rejection or
non-fulfilment falsifies it only when that evidence defeats that predicate.
Insufficient evidence remains indeterminate, an invalid governing basis is
invalid_basis, and an unsupported evaluation domain is out_of_frame.
An unsupported/rejected domain label without its reason cannot choose among
these cases. Performance and effects remain separate core coordinates.
Closed handling does not promise external-computation termination.

constraints.statement: Semantic functions should be total or as close as allowed. Bind admitted inputs, intended result and permitted continuation/repair/recovery/re-entry/refusal/yield/termination under Contract application and bounded construction; retain original outcomes in core returns. Prefer ingress rejection, admitted kernel carriers, closed Result-like outcomes and explicit validation/unsupported/rejected cases; avoid hidden preconditions, semantic .get fallback chains and defaults reconstructing missing truth. Evaluate the actual predicate: intended result supports satisfaction; rejection/non-fulfilment falsifies only when it defeats that predicate; insufficient evidence is indeterminate, invalid basis invalid_basis and unsupported evaluation domain out_of_frame. Unsupported/rejected labels without reasons decide none of these. Performance/effects remain separate; closed handling promises no external-computation termination.
constraints.uncertainty: Contract application and bounded construction are only referenced.

conditions: Effectful design and actual write/publication/invocation boundaries.

grounding.quote:
Bind the actual write, publication, invocation or other effect boundary to the
core effect record through
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application).
[Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) decides unknown
effect reconciliation and any dependent repeat on current owning state,
including after private context is discarded.

If a function both decides the semantic meaning and directly performs the write,
the design should be treated as suspect.

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit/isolated; examples are file writes, network calls, subprocesses, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation. Kernels should not perform these while deciding law. Prefer admitted/parsed authoritative input → typed plan/outcome → edge effects → downstream events/projections. Bind actual effect boundaries to core records via Contract application. Unknown-effect reconciliation and dependent repeat use current owning state under Workspace and context, even after private context loss. A function deciding semantics and directly writing should be treated as suspect.
constraints.uncertainty: The current-state reconciliation contract is not supplied.

conditions: Each controller, manager, service, loop or public wrapper, according to its declared role.

grounding.quote:
Apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application)
to each controller, manager, service, loop or public wrapper using its declared
role. Closure, identity, failure, next-work and current-truth determinations
must come from their admitted carriers, contracts or explicit design owners.
A wrapper that decides them through procedural orchestration, legacy fallbacks,
payload-fragment reconstruction or open-dictionary handling becomes an
undeclared semantic center and fails the authority/preservation conditions.

constraints.statement: Apply role-bound Contract application. Closure, identity, failure, next-work and current truth must derive from admitted carriers/contracts/explicit design owners. Wrappers deciding these through orchestration, legacy fallbacks, payload reconstruction or open dictionaries become undeclared semantic centers and fail authority/preservation conditions.

grounding.quote:
Design is too coupled when:

- many modules read and mutate the same object
- projections must inspect implementation state to infer truth
- a consumer can silently rebuild source truth from raw artifacts
- tests pass only because multiple modules still carry the same meaning

Reducing coupling means reducing the number of places where meaning can be
invented.

constraints.statement: Reduce coupling through dependency shape, not file count alone. Preferred direction is carriers → semantic kernels → effect shells → projections, rather than controllers → service helpers → mutable runtime state → projections. Excess coupling includes shared mutation by many modules, projections inferring truth from implementation state, consumers silently reconstructing source truth from raw artifacts, and tests passing only because several modules carry the same meaning. Reduction decreases places where meaning can be invented.
constraints.uncertainty: The arrows are retained as the source's preferred dependency direction, without inventing import or runtime-call semantics.

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
exceptions: Ratified responsibility explicitly including strategy ownership permits prescription within that role and actual grant.
Budgets/scores/counters/heuristics recreating another actor's judgment have an explicitly owned assessment-boundary exception.

grounding.quote:
Where ratified responsibility explicitly includes strategy ownership, the
boundary may prescribe strategy within that owned role and its actual grant.
Explicitly owned assessment retains the assessment-boundary exception below.
This rule's additional domain policy is the governance/strategy publication
distinction and the listed lawful and unlawful forms. F2/F4/F6 explain its
authority boundary; they do not select governance-only responsibility for every
system or grant strategy or assessment ownership.

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth rather than imperative strategy unless explicitly owned and granted. Responsibility/grants are instance premises. F2 separates information from prescription; F4 preserves actor responsibility/authority across handoffs; F6 separates evidence from permission. Lawful governance includes current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure/unresolved ids, eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, policy identity and continuity. Strategy drift includes downstream repair/action imperatives, preferences disguised as observability, unowned judgment-replacing metrics, and hidden doctrine in prompts/reports/read models. Systems intended to remain governance/observability must not become replacement decision engines through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers. F2/F4/F6 neither force governance-only responsibility universally nor grant strategy/assessment roles.

conditions: A realization boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic optimization is lawful only when it is:

- boundary-local to the active design or module surface
- behavior-preserving at the declared semantic boundary
- authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth
- visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads
- effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence, or
  bootstrap doctrine

constraints.statement: Opened areas should be improved, subordinate to constitutional truth, ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Lawful cleanup must be local, behavior-preserving, authority-neutral, visibility-neutral and effect-neutral. Examples include eliminating parser re-entry on locally assembled truth, consolidating local routes, improving local algorithms/scans with unchanged semantics, and simplifying fixtures/tests without changing module claims. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing, public carrier/visibility/truth-ownership changes, widened effects/observability, or performance changes to Product expectations require design re-entry. Cross-boundary discoveries are repricing inputs, never silently absorbed; authority-admitted follow-up enters separately at the smallest lawful point. This method owns scope separation; Ticket Method owns recording and closure mechanics.
constraints.uncertainty: Ticket follow-up rules are not supplied.

conditions: The same realization pattern appears across more than one processed boundary.
exceptions: A third local rebuild is conformant only if the boundary consumes an existing reusable surface, extends it before local implementation lands, or review records an explicit do-not-commonize decision with boundary-specific rationale.

grounding.quote:
The rule of two is:

- the second credible recurrence forces a library/commonization review
- the third local rebuild is not acceptable by default

A third local rebuild is not design-method conformant unless one of these is
true:

- the active boundary consumes an existing reusable library/commonization surface
- the active boundary extends that surface before the local implementation lands
- review records an explicit do-not-commonize decision and why the pattern is
  still boundary-specific

constraints.statement: Review recurrence as commonization, not merely local cleanup. A second credible recurrence forces library review; a third rebuild requires a listed exception. Ticket Method owns ticket enforcement/recording, including library_usage, governing_library and library_rationale. Prefer local cleanup, then tenant-local library, then shared propagation only through separate design re-entry. Tenant-local authority-neutral reusable patterns should be extracted. Changes to ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or shared law are separate design decisions. Commonization closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and superseded production responsibility is retired or satisfies Spec retention. Compare removed work and maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines and unused helpers do not prove contraction.
constraints.uncertainty: The Spec retention relation and ticket enforcement details are not supplied.

conditions: A ticket adopts the method and claims its boundary processed.
Before claiming design-method closure.
exceptions: The check may be ordinary ticket verification and requires no separate artifact, round or reviewer.
Current accepted evidence may be reused after exact scope, traces, applicability and invalidators are checked.

grounding.quote:
- an issue that falsifies the current claim or applicable hard stop blocks the
  design-method closure claim
- ticket or review wording cannot narrow applicable active authority away
- boundary-local cleanup or commonization is absorbed only when required to make
  the current claim true, preserve singular authority, satisfy accepted design,
  or avoid the durable architectural foreclosure above
- other cleanup, recurrence, generality, and cross-boundary opportunities are
  repricing inputs; they do not automatically widen the subject, block its
  bounded claim, or require a follow-up ticket
- any repricing admitted by the owning authority enters through the smallest
  lawful re-entry point

This rule keeps design closure truthful without turning discovery into automatic
scope expansion. Current defects and hard stops remain blocking. Useful
observations may survive as repricing input. Unclaimed future capability and
optional cleanup do not become implicit work.

constraints.statement: Check accepted design and exact closure claim rather than implementation status alone: boundary lawfulness; all causally applicable live requirements, accepted relations and retained predecessor claims; competing/ambiguous acceptance authority; durable architectural decisions foreclosing admitted Product outcomes; and defects falsifying the claim/hard stops. Reconstruct the complete selected function through requirements, Ontology, Prime, IACS, views, modules, implementation and module proof, not only prior findings. Hashes identify subjects, headings/artifacts locate, and green tests prove only assertions; none supplies missing relations or weaker substitutes. Causal closure is of the declared claim, not the whole Product/history. New reviewers/conversations do not force reauthoring; missing/stale/ambiguous coverage is not no-delta proof. Material change/counterexample requires affected reconstruction/gate while retaining unaffected support. Blocking defects/hard stops stay blocking; wording cannot narrow active authority. Absorb cleanup/commonization only when needed for truth, singular authority, accepted design or avoiding durable foreclosure. Other opportunities are repricing, not automatic scope/blockers/follow-up tickets; admitted work enters minimally. Ticket Method retains status, closure, reopening, dependencies and follow-up ownership.
constraints.uncertainty: The applicable live requirements and Ticket Method are not provided for any concrete ticket.

conditions: A crossing between interface families.
Faithful projection additionally applies when the consumer is a view.

grounding.quote:
For a crossing between interface families, apply
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to their
declared source and consumer roles; apply Faithful projection when the consumer
is a view. Each family has its authoritative source, and downstream interfaces
consume it. Projection-to-closure, report/prompt-to-admission,
wrapper-to-kernel and adapter-to-semantic-owner changes are undeclared authority
transfers, not ordinary interface translation. This is semantic non-bleed;
smaller functions alone do not establish it.

constraints.statement: Apply contracts to declared source/consumer roles; each family's downstream interfaces consume its authoritative source. Projection-to-closure, report/prompt-to-admission, wrapper-to-kernel and adapter-to-semantic-owner changes are undeclared authority transfers, not translations. Smaller functions alone do not prove non-bleed.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete Contract application and Faithful projection contracts are outside the supplied material.

conditions: Projects using this method.
exceptions: Intentionally retained compatibility must be an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof.

grounding.quote:
If compatibility is intentionally retained, it must be treated as an explicit
feature with its own bounded authority and proof.

Otherwise the proxy path must be removed.

constraints.statement: Proxy or partial interface implementations must not substitute for real migration/design completion. Retained compatibility requires its explicit bounded feature authority/proof; otherwise remove the proxy path.

conditions: Review of the exact adopted boundary and claim.
exceptions: Python typing evidence is conditional on Python; ODD/UX specialization is conditional on the applicable surface.

grounding.quote:
Review the exact adopted boundary and claim by applying
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application).
Acquire the applicable owners below with the actual design and implementation.
The table selects the required decision evidence; it is not another definition
